results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the undeclared var.env reference in main.tf line 12 and recommends changing it back to var.environment, matching the answer key; the rename-the-declaration alternative appears only as a conditional next check, not a wrong fix.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit b756522 on fail/bad-terraform changed sample-app/infra/main.tf line 12 from `var.environment` to `var.env`, but only `environment` and `instance_count` are declared, so `terraform validate` fails on a reference to an undeclared input variable.
key_evidence: [10:53:24] Error: Reference to undeclared input variable
[10:53:24] An input variable with the name "env" has not been declared. This variable
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/infra/main.tf line 12, change the reference back to `app_name = "calculator-${var.environment}"` so it uses the declared `environment` variable (default "dev").
assumptions: No file in sample-app/infra/ other than main.tf declares variables. The git-investigator could not list the infra/ file tree because Bash was blocked, and inferred this from the branch changing only main.tf.
next_checks: Run `terraform validate` in sample-app/infra after the change to confirm the error is gone.
If the rename to `env` was intended, rename the `variable "environment"` declaration to `env` instead, and update every caller that sets `environment` through `-var` or `TF_VAR_environment`.
Check that the planned resource names (calculator-dev-1, calculator-dev-2) match what main produces.

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies subtract() returning a + b as the cause of the test failure (14 != 6) and recommends reverting it to a - b without touching the test, matching the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 4446cb4 ("Refactor calculator arithmetic helpers") changed subtract() in sample-app/app/calculator.py from `return a - b` to `return a + b`, so subtract(10, 4) returns 14 and fails the unchanged, correct assertion in test_subtract.
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/app/calculator.py, change the body of subtract() back to `return a - b` (as on main). Leave tests/test_calculator.py unchanged.
next_checks: Run `python -m pytest -v` in sample-app after the fix and confirm all 5 tests pass.
Check that the rest of the 'Refactor calculator arithmetic helpers' commit did not mean to change behavior anywhere else (the diff shows only this one line changed).

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the missing 'deploy-token' credential in Jenkins as the cause, notes the README commit is unrelated, and suggests re-creating the credential with no code changes, matching the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: Jenkins has no credential with ID 'deploy-token' that the calculator job can see, so withCredentials in the Deploy stage failed. The branch's only change (a new README) is unrelated; the Jenkinsfile matches main.
key_evidence: ERROR: Could not find credentials entry with ID 'deploy-token'
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In Jenkins (Manage Jenkins > Credentials), create or restore a 'Secret text' credential with the exact ID 'deploy-token' at global scope, or at the calculator folder's scope. Then rebuild the branch. Leave the Jenkinsfile and the branch unchanged.
assumptions: The credential is missing or at the wrong scope in the jenkins_home volume. Nobody looked at the Jenkins credential store directly.
The credential was there before (other builds of main passed Deploy). The reports don't confirm this.
next_checks: Look in the Jenkins credential store (global and the calculator folder scope) for an entry with ID 'deploy-token'. Check for typos, a deleted entry or the wrong scope.
Make sure the credential type is 'Secret text', since the Jenkinsfile uses the string() binding.
Check whether recent builds of main also fail at Deploy, which would confirm the problem is in the environment.
Find out whether the jenkins_home volume was recreated or reset recently, which would remove credentials added through the UI.

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the misspelled credentialsId 'deploy-tokn' and recommends changing it back to 'deploy-token' in sample-app/Jenkinsfile, which matches the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 4a1b8a2 on fail/missing-credential changed the Deploy stage's withCredentials ID from 'deploy-token' to the misspelled 'deploy-tokn'. No credential with that ID exists in Jenkins, so the binding failed before the deploy command ran.
key_evidence: ERROR: Could not find credentials entry with ID 'deploy-tokn'
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/Jenkinsfile on the Deploy stage, change credentialsId: 'deploy-tokn' back to credentialsId: 'deploy-token' to match main.
assumptions: A credential with ID 'deploy-token' exists in the Jenkins credential store. Main building green suggests it does, but the store was not checked directly.
The rename to 'deploy-tokn' was an accidental typo, not a planned switch to a new credential that was never created.
next_checks: In Jenkins (Manage Jenkins > Credentials), confirm that 'deploy-token' exists and 'deploy-tokn' does not.
Ask the author of commit 4a1b8a2 whether they meant to change the credential ID.
After fixing the ID, check that the Deploy stage prints the token-length line and the build finishes SUCCESS.

results.judge_explanation: The diagnosis identifies the 3→90 SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS change exceeding the 1-minute stage timeout, and its primary fix restores the default to 3 while keeping the timeout, matching the answer key.

diagnosis.root_cause: Commit 220b4ad on fail/timeout raised the default SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS in sample-app/scripts/smoke_test.py from 3 to 90 seconds, but the Smoke Test stage has a 1-minute timeout. Jenkins killed the stage after 60s, before the 90s wait could finish.
key_evidence: [10:54:12] Timeout set to expire in 1 min 0 sec
[10:54:13] Waiting 90s for the service to become healthy...
[10:55:12] Cancelling nested steps due to timeout
diagnosis.suggested_fix: In sample-app/scripts/smoke_test.py, set the default back to WAIT_SECONDS = int(os.environ.get("SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS", "3")), as on main. Keep the stage timeout as it is. Any environment that truly needs a longer wait can set SMOKE_WAIT_SECONDS explicitly, to a value below the stage timeout.
assumptions: No environment the pipeline runs in actually needs more than 3s for the service to become healthy; the commit message says 'slower environments', but no evidence names one.
With a 3s wait the smoke test passes, as it does on main; the log never shows the health check succeeding or failing.
next_checks: Ask the commit author which slower environment led to the 90s change, and whether it needs a longer wait at all.
If a longer wait is really needed, raise the Smoke Test stage timeout above the wait (with some margin), and note this is a deliberate change.
Look into the slow pytest collection (~97s, 10:52:32 to 10:54:09) reported by the log-reader; it is unrelated to this failure but unusual.
